column1: # Columns: match<TAB>key<TAB>behaviour<TAB>note. Rules are tried in this order
# for one package: `package` (exact name), `unloaded` (UnloadedPlatoonJob of the
# package or its nearest ancestor), `keyword` (substring of the package name,
# then of its ancestors', file order). Nothing matches: generic fallback.
# Behaviours implemented: travel, go_home, stay_home, patrol_local,
# animal_territory, raid, man_the_gate, trade_circuit, shop_keeper, resident_life, bar_hangout, guard_shift, cage_warden.
# Any other name is "planned": the squad runs the fallback
# and the coverage report counts it.
# `unloaded` comes first because it is the original's own abstract-behaviour
# field; `keyword` rows cover the packages that set it to NONE (79 of 219).
# `package` rows pin the cases where the field disagrees with the package's
# goals (the original only travels or patrols abstractly while unloaded; our
# squads live their ordinary life at every level, so the goals are the intent).
# Guard packages: UNSURE field, clear goals. Their unloaded func is
# TRAVEL_TARGET but their goals are GO_HOME_AND_GO_TO_BED, MAN_A_TURRET,
# INVESTIGATE_ALARMS, ATTACK_TROUBLE_MAKERS (shift posts: none travels or
# patrols), and Task_PatrolTown has no loop of its own (it follows the
# package's target; docs/reference/tasks/Task_PatrolTown.md). So they hold the
# post: guard_shift (T3e1; the scorer runs the halves' windows and the intruder
# pickup). "Guard military patrol base" does list PATROL_TOWN: it patrols.
